title: Reorder a prompt so most of it is served from cache, with the answers unchanged
problem:
Providers bill a cached prefix at a fraction of the normal input price, and the cache only holds while the beginning of the prompt is byte identical. Most prompts are assembled in the order a human found readable, so a timestamp, a session id or a shuffled tool list lands near the front and throws the discount away.
The task is mechanical and the payoff is immediate: rearrange the prompt so the stable part comes first and the volatile part last, without changing a single answer.

acceptance.how:
Your repo runs `make eval` over a fixed set of at least 50 prompts named in the README, twice in a row against one provider. It prints JSON: {cache_read_fraction, answers_identical, n}. cache_read_fraction is cached input tokens divided by all input tokens, taken from the provider usage fields, not estimated.
A verifier sends cache_read_fraction as the score and confirms answers_identical equals n on the same run. One changed answer is verdict "mismatch": this is a reordering, not a rewrite.
acceptance.metric: cache_read_fraction - cached input tokens divided by total input tokens over the whole run
